chapter: Piano craft and the New York school
title: How Tatum made an out-of-tune piano sound good
summary: He explains how the pianist played in between the cracks on poorly tuned instruments, relative pitch, and piano as a fixed-tone instrument.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Who played piano: the pianists musicians remembered

blocks.x: Well, it was a challenge for him to make a dated piano sound good.
Well, how did he do that?
He seemed to get a kick out of that.
...getting a kick out of making a poor piano sound good.

Well, number one, if the piano was bad, he would play a nickelodeon type piano. You know what I mean? He'd play a blues, things like that to give it that ring-a-ming-a-dink-a-dink! But now, if he could get something else out of the piano, could get it halfway tuned in a couple of keys, he would try to... I'm not saying he played wrecks, because he wouldn't play on a wreck. I'm talking about a piano that's not actually tuned, that's not a Steinway or...
Right. Well, that place he used to play in...

Now, here's the thing... I don't think he ha actual pitch. I think he had relative pitch. Because some pianists, like say Ellis Larkins, wonderful...he has a very fine, refined touch on the piano... It bothers him to play the chords and play them... He (?) them to establish his expression on the piano. And since the piano is out of

tune, below par, below 440, it bothers the ear. Not only of him, but people that have... So that he would play... To make up for the lack of tonality, sometimes he'd play the harmony a half-tone below, and he'll try to play a tone above on the melody.

You know, it's a cliche amongst young people about playing between the cracks. Well, actually it is (?) to play in between the way the piano is tempered. Now, it's a fixed instrument; piano is a fixed instrument, you know. Of course, a trombone, violin and the voice, you don't have any fixed tonality there. You can...
